newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian budget seen boosting air cargo.
newsitem.headline: Indian budget seen boosting air cargo.

text.p: The Indian budget has cut duty right across the electronics and information technology board, promising to boost air cargo imports and exports, industry sources told Reuters.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told Parliament on February 28 that the top rate of customs duty will be cut to 40 percent from from 50 percent and within three years there should only be a four rate structure to match that ASEAN countries.

The freight and tour industry has also criticised the proposal to extend the five percent tax on the service sector to the transport of goods by road, custom house operations, steamer, clearing and forwarding agents, air travel agents, tour operators and car rental agencies, the sources said.

Indian Airlines general manager cargo, Anita Khurana told Reuters the increase in rail freight rates by some 12.5 percent in the Rail budget earlier last will shift a small amount of business, such as courier parcels, off the railways to air and they would be happy to get it.

Budget details included import duty removed on computer software; duty on computer parts drops to 10 percent from 20 percent, except for printed circuit boards which drop to 20 percent from 30 percent, while integrated circuits go to 10 percent from 20 percent.
Import duty on colour monitor tubes has been reduced to 10 percent from 20 percent and duty on colour tv picture tubes to 30 percent from 35 percent.

Another move was to cut the tariff on parts for cellular phones and pagers to 20 percent from 30 percent. However, a Finance ministry official said that, contrary to first budget reports, import duty on ready-assembled cellular phones and pagers remains at 30 percent.

Duty on telecoms equipment moves to 30 percent from 40 percent and telecom equipment parts to 20 percent from 30 percent. Watch parts and movements drop to 20 percent duty from 50 percent, with that on base metal watch cases dropping to 30 percent from 50 percent.
Duty on digital video disk drives is down to 10 percent from 20 percent. However domestic excise duty on video cassette recorders and players excise duty was raised to 18 percent from 15 percent.

The import duty on specified food items used by hotels for foreign tourists drops to 25 percent from 50 percent. Cine film and other photgraphic film drops to 25 percent from 30 percent and on camera parts to 25 percent from 50 percent .

Samsung deputy MD India, R.K. Caprihan, said that the consumer electronics sector could almost double its growth rate after the budget cuts which could produce a drop in prices of five to seven percent across the sector.

Industry sources added that a secret Indian project was nearing completion, with a prototype already tested, of a domestically built and designed GSM cellular phone to would retail at between 30 percent and 50 percent of the cost of foreign phones.
This could be a serious domestic and export challenge for foreign firms, they said.
For computers, which have seen falling prices, dedicated export manufacturers will now be allowed to sell up to 50 percent of their production into the domestic market.

At the same time, while Indian entrepreneurs have generally complained that they lack a level playing field vis a vis foreign products, the software industry reaction to zero duty on imports is that competition will spur the domestic market to produce and export more. - Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
